description: We're a Full-Stack & AI duo teaming up from Argentina and Spain. Using React, Next.js, Angular, TypeScript, Python (FastAPI), and AWS/Cloudflare, we build end-to-end apps—from AI/RAG pipelines and Three.js 3D interfaces to enterprise dashboards and Cypress QA. Working across American and European time zones ensures continuous sprint progress and clear C1 English pitching. We're competing as a closed two-person squad and aren't seeking new members.
summary: Marswalk Planner is a static, browser-based tool for planning a safe human traverse across Jezero Crater for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It combines NASA’s 20 m CTX terrain model, HiRISE imagery, Perseverance’s traverse and MEDA weather data in one layered map. The user sets a start, destination and science stops; a slope-aware A* planner returns distance, ascent, walking time, maximum slope, energy and oxygen use, and checks whether the crew can still walk back. Terrain-risk warnings, an elevation profile, six science stops, comparison with the rover’s actual route and an emergency-return mode make the plan explainable rather than a black box. Everything runs client-side and the interface works on phones and tablets, so it is usable in the field or for outreach. It matters because future crews will have limited daylight, oxygen and energy: integrating terrain, environment and science priorities into one clear plan reduces risk and helps teams justify why a route is safe.
details:
• What it does / How it works: Marswalk Planner allows users to plan, analyze, and safety-check walking routes on Mars. Users can select preset routes (e.g., Landing to Three Forks or Bright Angel) or interactively set custom start, stop, and destination coordinates on a detailed HiRISE/MOLA map of Jezero Crater. The app uses an asynchronous Web Worker running an A* pathfinding algorithm over a 600x600 grid (20-meter resolution) that evaluates local slopes using Tobler’s hiking function and blocks paths exceeding a 30° incline.
    • Frontend: React 18, Vite, Leaflet 1.9.4, Plain CSS.
    • Algorithms / Workers: Web Workers for A* route calculation and Dijkstra-based emergency return pathfinding.
    • Data Processing & Formats: GeoJSON, Binary elevation and slope buffers (.bin), and custom JSON datasets.
  • Creativity and Factors Considered: Unlike generic mapping tools, Marswalk Planner incorporates real Martian environmental constraints: atmospheric MEDA weather limits (minimum temperatures, solar radiation), Perseverance rover traverse comparisons as a structural sanity check, and realistic energy expenditures adjusted for Mars' gravity.

GitHub: https://github.com/LeonAntGon/marswall-planner
